data.name: Agnes 3.0 Flash
data.description: Agnes 3.0 Flash is designed for real-world agent tasks and development workflows, covering the full execution chain from task understanding and planning to tool invocation and final delivery. The model focuses on improving stability, instruction-following, factual grounding, and output completeness in complex tasks, with vision in and text out via an OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions interface.

data.name: Claude Fable 5.1
data.description: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 is the successor to Claude Fable 5 for long-running agentic coding, knowledge work, and research. Same $10/$50 list rates as Fable 5, with cache reads at $0.25 per million tokens and a 1M-token context window.

data.name: Claude Haiku 5.5
data.description: Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5 is the fastest and most cost-efficient model in the Claude 5.x lineup. It delivers instant responsiveness for lightweight tasks, supports tool use and function calling, and features 1M-token context with vision input. Built for rapid ideation, summarization, and classification at low cost. Adaptive thinking always on.

data.name: Claude Opus 5.5
data.description: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 is the successor to Claude Opus 5 for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work. It delivers Fable 5.1-level performance at 40% lower cost ($4 / $20 per million input / output tokens), with adaptive thinking always on, 1M-token context, vision input, and tool use. Built for multi-step changes in large codebases, code review and bug finding, financial and scientific analysis, and reading dense charts and diagrams.

data.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
data.description: Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 5.5 is the successor to Claude Sonnet 5 — the best combination of speed and intelligence in the lineup. It is the direct upgrade for well-scoped everyday work (building features, fixing bugs, drafting and review) at the same $2 / $10 per million input / output rates, with adaptive thinking on by default at `high` effort, 1M-token context, 128K max output, vision input, and tool use. Faster than Opus 5.5, cheaper, same window.

data.name: Apodex 1.1 Mini
data.description: Apodex 1.1 Mini is a reasoning-first model from Apodex, built for complex, long-horizon research and forecasting tasks. It works directly with files, data, code, and tools to produce verifiable results, with text in and text out. Served through the Novita BYOK route; OpenRouter lists no endpoints.

data.name: Quyet 1.0 Large
data.description: Quyet-1.0-Large is a calibrated decision model by Chinh Nguyen, fine-tuned from Google Gemma-4-31B-it: it reads a state (text, JSON, or a conversation) and a typed question, and returns one option with calibrated probabilities — not generated chat text. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: Laya
data.description: Laya is Convai Innovations' System One evaluation model: send shared state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get structured answers with probabilities in one forward pass — not generated chat text. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
data.description: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 is the October 17, 2026 snapshot of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, served by DeepSeek under the `deepseek-flash` API model name. Sparse mixture-of-experts with native vision in, text out, and a 1M-token context window. Hosts bill it as its own model: OpenRouter lists it at $0.15 / $0.60 per 1M input / output tokens, against $0.04 / $0.144 for the original September checkpoint `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`.

data.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
data.description: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash is the cost-efficient sparse MoE tier of the V4.1 family, built on the Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED) architecture: 552B total parameters with 8B active on input and 16B on output. Native vision in, text out, 1M context. Compressed KV cache needs roughly a quarter of the previous Flash's HBM. This is the original September 2026 checkpoint, listed by OpenRouter as `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`. The official API id `deepseek-flash` now serves the October 17 snapshot, which has its own listing `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`.

data.name: GLiNER2.5-Decide
data.description: Fastino GLiNER2.5-Decide is a decision model: send application state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get structured answers with confidence — not generated chat text. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler). Upstream, GLiNER2.5 runs schema-driven classifications on an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API; the gateway adapts the System One envelope for this hop.

data.name: Ember-1
data.description: Ember-1 is a reasoning model from Fireworks Research built on Kimi K3. It is tuned to produce shorter reasoning traces, with tool use, image input, and a 1M-token context window.

data.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
data.description: Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash is a multimodal model for fast agentic workflows, coding, and complex multi-step reasoning, with a 1,048,576-token context window.

data.name: THX-01
data.description: THX-01 is a 322M multilingual decision model from HAL-X AI, trained with reinforcement learning on a strictly proper scoring rule so its probabilities are calibrated. Send a state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get an answer with probabilities for each question in one forward pass of about 10 ms — not generated chat text. Post-trained in 18 languages, 100+ supported. Apache 2.0. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: Mercury 2.5
data.description: Inception Labs' Mercury 2.5 is a diffusion language model for fast text generation and reasoning, with a 260,000-token context window.

data.name: Mercury Decide
data.description: Mercury Decide is Inception's structured decision model. Send application state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get back a choice, a score, or a yes/no answer, each with a calibrated probability taken straight from the model rather than written out as text, so no output tokens are generated. It answers up to 14 decisions per second, which is fast enough to run on every case and escalate only the unsure ones. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: Ling-3.0-flash-Sante
data.description: Ling-3.0-flash-Sante is inclusionAI's health and medicine-focused mixture-of-experts model, built on Ling-3.0-flash (124B total / 5.1B active). It is designed for medical knowledge reasoning, clinical safety, evidence-based retrieval, and long-horizon medical tasks, while retaining general reasoning, coding, and agentic skills. Distinct from text-only inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash and the VL listing. BYOK only: OpenRouter withdrew the :free SKU and Nous Portal 404s it, so the platform free pool no longer serves it. Command Code lists the same product as a free-while-it-lasts promo — that is the upstream's credit, not AnyRouter Free monthly credits.

data.name: Ling-3.0-flash-VL
data.description: Ling-3.0-flash-VL is inclusionAI's native multimodal instruct model, a 124B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with roughly 5.5B activated parameters per token. Built on Ling-3.0-flash, it adds native image and video understanding (up to 256K context) for visual reasoning, document and chart reading, and agentic GUI tasks. Distinct from the text-only inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash listing. OpenRouter withdrew the :free SKU, so there is no platform free pool left and this listing is BYOK-only on the paid OpenRouter slug; the `:free` id remains an alias for it.

data.name: Ling-3.1-flash
data.description: Ling 3.1 Flash is a hybrid reasoning mixture-of-experts model from inclusionAI, with 25B active parameters out of 560B total. Nous Portal platform hop is paid ($0.075/$0.225 per 1M, repriced by Nous 2026-10-16); the OpenRouter platform hop is commented out (#4527) after 402-ing on every attempt, and Novita/OpenRouter/Command Code/Vercel BYOK hops serve it at $0.

data.name: Kev 4B
data.description: Kev 4B is a small open-weight decision model from Jared Palmer — a LoRA adapter and pointer head on Qwen3.5-4B-Base. Send state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get a calibrated probability per question in one forward pass, not generated text. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: Liquid d1
data.description: Liquid d1 is Liquid AI's first decision model: send application state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get calibrated probabilities back in a single call with zero generated tokens — not chat text. Built for classification, routing, scoring, moderation and guardrails. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: LFM 2.5 24B A2B
data.description: Liquid AI LFM2.5-24B-A2B is an open-weight reasoning mixture-of-experts model with 24B total and about 2B active parameters per token. It always reasons before it answers and is built for fast agents, tool use and structured output, with a 128K context window.

data.name: LongCat-2.5-Preview
data.description: LongCat-2.5-Preview is Meituan's sparse mixture-of-experts frontier model — ~1.6T total parameters with ~48B active — over a 1M-token context window. It adds native multimodal understanding (image input), stronger coding ability, and a `thinking` toggle, and is built for long-horizon agentic work across terminals, browsers, GUIs, spreadsheets, and design tools. Served over the OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic-compatible APIs.

data.name: Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor
data.description: The cost-efficient contributor tier of Meta's multimodal reasoning model Muse Spark 1.3, for experimentation and early-stage agentic and coding workflows.

data.name: Muse Spark 1.3
data.description: Meta's Muse Spark 1.3 is a multimodal reasoning model for complex agentic tasks. It accepts text, images, video, audio, and PDF documents, returns text, and offers a 1M-token context window.

data.name: Muse Spark Open
data.description: Meta's Muse Spark Open is a coding-optimized open-weight model for agentic coding. It is a sparse mixture-of-experts with 816B total and about 42B active parameters, reads text, images, video, audio and files, returns text, and has a 1M-token context window.

data.name: Muse Wonder
data.description: Meta's Muse Wonder is a frontier reasoning model for complex personal and professional agentic tasks. It accepts text, images, video, audio and PDF documents and returns text.

data.name: Microsoft-Decision-1
data.description: Microsoft-Decision-1 is a small Microsoft model built for fast decisions: yes/no, multiple-choice and rating questions, plus rubric-based grading of AI responses and agent actions. Send application state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get back a calibrated probability for each fixed answer option, not generated chat text. It has a 32,768-token context window. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
data.description: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash is a multimodal model from MiniMax. Compared with M3, it improves across benchmarks, particularly complex agentic tasks, coding and cybersecurity. It is built for multi-step co-work automation, understanding real codebases, fixing bugs and building features, and for visual understanding and creation, including frontend and presentation work. It has a 1M token context window and always-on reasoning with adjustable effort.

data.name: Mistral Large 4
data.description: Mistral Large 4 is Mistral AI's frontier model for reasoning, coding, and agentic work, with text and image input, tool use, structured output, and a context window of up to 1M tokens.

data.name: Drex v1.5
data.description: Drex v1.5 is a small decision model from Nace AI, served over the same System One contract as TypeSafe's Jev. Send application state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get back a calibrated probability for each fixed answer option, not generated chat text. It has a 131,072-token context window. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: Drex v2.0
data.description: Drex v2.0 is a 35B mixture-of-experts decision model (3B active) from Nace AI, the larger successor to Drex v1.5. Send application state (text or JSON) and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get back a calibrated probability for every answer option in a single forward pass, with no text generation. It is TypeSafe System One compatible and suits routing, classification and policy checks that need a scored answer instead of prose. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: Nex-N2.5-Mini
data.description: Nex-N2.5-Mini is Nex AGI's smaller agentic coding model (35B total / 3B active MoE), built for high-speed instruction following, real-time tool execution, and visually assisted computer use. Distinct from Nex-N2.5-Pro and the retired Nex-N2-Pro listing. OpenRouter withdrew the :free SKU in September 2026, so the platform free pool is gone and this listing is BYOK-only; both the paid OpenRouter slug and the old :free id resolve here.

data.name: Nex-N2.5-Pro
data.description: Nex-N2.5-Pro is Nex AGI's larger agentic coding model (397B total / 17B active MoE), built to turn goals into working, verified outcomes with a visual feedback loop. Distinct from Nex-N2.5-Mini and the retired Nex-N2-Pro listing. OpenRouter withdrew the :free SKU in September 2026, so the platform free pool is gone and this listing is BYOK-only; both the paid OpenRouter slug and the old :free id resolve here.

data.name: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B A12B
data.description: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a vision-language model for reasoning, coding, tool use, document understanding and video understanding. A hybrid Mamba-2 and Transformer mixture-of-experts with 120B total and 12B active parameters, and up to 1M tokens of context.

data.name: GPT-6 Astra Pro
data.description: GPT-6 Astra served with reasoning mode set to pro for higher-quality answers on complex tasks. Pro mode spends far more reasoning tokens than standard GPT-6 Astra.

data.name: GPT-6 Astra
data.description: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra reasoning/chat model with ~1.05M context; Experiential Cloud promotional free daily tier.

data.name: GPT-6 Luna Pro
data.description: GPT-6 Luna served with reasoning mode set to pro for higher-quality answers on complex tasks. Pro mode spends far more reasoning tokens than standard GPT-6 Luna.

data.name: GPT-6 Luna
data.description: OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna is the efficient GPT-6 tier for focused, high-throughput tasks, with configurable reasoning, tool use, image input, and a 1.05M-token context window.

data.name: GPT-6 Sol Pro
data.description: GPT-6 Sol served with reasoning mode set to pro for higher-quality answers on complex tasks. Pro mode spends far more reasoning tokens than standard GPT-6 Sol.

data.name: GPT-6 Sol
data.description: OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol is built for complex coding and agentic workflows, with configurable reasoning, tool use, image input, and a 1.05M-token context window. It is the high-end GPT-6 tier below GPT-6 Astra.

data.name: GPT-6.1 Sol Pro
data.description: GPT-6.1 Sol served with reasoning mode set to pro for higher-quality answers on complex tasks. Pro mode spends far more reasoning tokens than standard GPT-6.1 Sol.

data.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
data.description: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol delivers near-Astra performance for complex coding and agentic work at a lower cost, with configurable reasoning, tool use, image input, and a 1.05M-token context window.

data.name: PPLX Decider v1 (27B)
data.description: PPLX Decider v1 (27B) is Perplexity's multimodal decision model: send application state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get back a probability distribution over a fixed set of answers — it returns probabilities, not generated chat text, and produces no free-form output. `state` may be a string, an object, or an array of OpenAI-style `image_url` parts carrying base64 PNG/JPEG/WebP data URLs, so it also scores images. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: PPLX Decider v1.1 (27B)
data.description: PPLX Decider v1.1 (27B) is a newer checkpoint of Perplexity's multimodal decision model, with the same Decisions API contract as v1: send application state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get back a probability distribution over a fixed set of answers — it returns probabilities, not generated chat text, and produces no free-form output. `state` may be a string, an object, or an array of OpenAI-style `image_url` parts carrying base64 PNG/JPEG/WebP data URLs, so it also scores images. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: Ternary Bonsai 2 27B
data.description: Bonsai 2 27B is PrismML's 27B reasoning model derived from Qwen3.8-27B and compressed to ternary weights. It supports coding, math, tool calling, and image input with a 262K-token context window.

data.name: Qwen3.8 Max Prime
data.description: A higher-throughput variant of Qwen3.8 Max from Alibaba's Qwen team, served as a separate SKU at a higher price. Accepts text, image and video input.

data.name: Beam 1.0
data.description: Beam 1.0 is Reflection's open-weights mixture-of-experts model — 501B total parameters, 23B active across 256 experts — built for token-efficient reasoning, agentic tool use, and software-engineering workloads. Reasoning is always on with a tunable effort level; the Apache-2.0 weights are on Hugging Face.

data.name: Span-01 Lite
data.description: Span-01 Lite is a behavior-scoring classifier from Respan — the free, lighter tier of Span-01, a 4B model trained with RLAIF on classification reasoning rather than fixed taxonomies. Send a conversation span and a set of plain-language behavior definitions and get a present / absent / not_observable probability per behavior in a single forward pass, with no token-by-token generation. Respan reports it ahead of Jev 1.13 and Sonnet 5 on their English and multilingual behavior-detection suites. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: Span-01
data.description: Span-01 is a behavior-scoring classifier from Respan, a 4B model trained with RLAIF on classification reasoning rather than fixed taxonomies. Send a conversation span and a set of plain-language behavior definitions and get a present / absent / not_observable probability per behavior in a single forward pass, with no token-by-token generation. It is the full tier of the family; Span-01 Lite is the lighter tier. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: Fugu Max
data.description: Fugu Max is the largest tier of Sakana AI's Fugu line — a 1M-token-context model that takes text, images, and files and returns text. It joins sakana/fugu and sakana/fugu-ultra as a distinct tier, and is not a v2 of fugu-ultra (that one is folded into the existing row as an alias, not a new listing).

data.name: Fugu Ultra v2
data.description: The higher-performance model in Sakana AI's Fugu family, a learned multi-agent orchestration system.

data.name: Amos 1 Large
data.description: Amos 1 Large is an open-weight (Apache 2.0) decision model from Scira: a 27B decoder fine-tuned from Qwen3.8-27B and Scira's most capable decision model, for multi-step questions, long policies and trade-offs. Context 128K tokens; about 122 ms median server time. Send a state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get a calibrated probability per answer in one pass — not generated chat text. English only. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler). Scira trains on every request, so it is skipped when Always enforce ZDR is on (Dashboard → Privacy).

data.name: Amos 1 Mini
data.description: Amos 1 Mini is an open-weight (Apache 2.0) decision model from Scira: a 0.5B encoder that answers every question in one pass on a CPU — simple decisions where the answer is in the case. Reads 9K tokens per pass; about 27 ms median server time. Send a state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get a calibrated probability per answer in one pass — not generated chat text. English only. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler). Scira trains on every request, so it is skipped when Always enforce ZDR is on (Dashboard → Privacy).

data.name: Amos 1 Small
data.description: Amos 1 Small is an open-weight (Apache 2.0) decision model from Scira: a 2B decoder fine-tuned from Qwen3.5-2B, built for volume and for cases with photos. Context 256K tokens; about 48 ms median server time. Send a state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get a calibrated probability per answer in one pass — not generated chat text. English only. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler). Scira trains on every request, so it is skipped when Always enforce ZDR is on (Dashboard → Privacy).

data.name: Glyph Cluster
data.description: Glyph Cluster is a reasoning model designed for coding and long-context workloads. It is a stealth preview model from a third-party provider who has chosen to remain anonymous during this preview. Free during stealth for Pro/Enterprise Vercel users and on Kilo's anonymous free tier. Text-only input; function calling supported; no structured outputs; no ZDR (prompts may be used for training).

data.name: Space Bunny Alpha
data.description: Space Bunny Alpha is an anonymous frontier-class model with blazing-fast inference, strong coding capabilities, and native multimodal input (text, image, video) with text out. It always reasons with adjustable reasoning effort over a 1M-token context window. Free while cloaked.

data.name: Step 5 Preview
data.description: Step 5 Preview is StepFun's next-generation flagship base model designed for real-world tasks, with a focus on programming and professional expertise. A multimodal (text, image, video in / text out) base model with a 1M-token context and adjustable reasoning effort.

data.name: Strands Decider 2B
data.description: Strands Decider 2B is AWS Strands Labs' small open-weight decision model: send application state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get calibrated probabilities back in one forward pass — it returns answers with confidence scores, not generated chat text, and produces no free-form output. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: SubQ Snap Preview
data.description: SubQ Snap Preview is Subquadratic's System One decision model for routing, guardrails, triage and other fast decisions. It is in public preview. Send application state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get back typed answers with probabilities and confidence — not generated chat text. SubQ documents text input and output plus image input (PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 4 images). Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: Jev
data.description: TypeSafe Jev is a decision model: send application state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get structured answers with probabilities — not generated chat text. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: Pareto 26.10 Preview
data.description: Pareto 26.10 Preview is Unbiased's newer composite model — it blends several language models into one answer, takes text and image input, and returns text over a 1,048,576-token context window (131,072 max completion). It is aimed at research, coding, and agentic workflows and is priced well under the current unbiased/pareto ($0.80 vs $2.50 per 1M input, $3.20 vs $7.50 per 1M output). A distinct, official OpenRouter listing — not a repack of the older unbiased/pareto row, which stays a disabled Cloudflare tombstone (#3368).

data.name: Solar Decide Flash
data.description: Upstage Solar Decide Flash is the low-latency variant of Solar Decide, a decision model served as a System One endpoint on Solar Mini 4: send application state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get structured answers back — not generated chat text. It has a 524,288-token context window. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: Solar Decide
data.description: Upstage Solar Decide is a decision model served as a System One endpoint on Solar Mini 4: send application state and typed questions (noul / choice / score) and get structured answers back — not generated chat text. It has a 524,288-token context window. Call POST /api/v1/decisions (POST /api/v1/systemone is the same handler).

data.name: Solar Mini 4
data.description: Solar Mini 4 is Upstage's small, fast tier in the Solar 4 generation: a text-only model with a 524,288-token context window at roughly $0.05 / $0.20 per million input / output tokens. It is the cheap sibling of upstage/solar-pro4, not a packaging of it, so it gets its own listing row.

data.name: Grok 4.7
data.description: SpaceXAI's frontier model for coding, agentic tasks, and knowledge work — succeeds Grok 4.6 with mandatory adjustable reasoning (low/medium/high/xhigh, default high).

data.name: MiMo V2.6 Flash
data.description: MiMo V2.6 Flash is Xiaomi's full-modality reasoning model for high-frequency invocations and large-scale professional workloads. It keeps the 1M-token context window and up to 128K output tokens of MiMo V2.6 Pro at roughly a third of the input price, making it the best-balanced pick when reasoning quality matters more than peak capability.

data.name: MiMo-V2.6-Pro UltraSpeed
data.description: The fast edition of Xiaomi's flagship MiMo-V2.6-Pro, built from the same 1T checkpoint with roughly 10x faster output.

data.name: MiMo V2.6 Pro
data.description: MiMo V2.6 Pro is Xiaomi's trillion-parameter, natively omni-modal flagship reasoning model for complex projects, long-horizon agentic tasks, coding, research, and professional knowledge work. It supports a 1M-token context window with up to 128K output tokens, and keeps the V2.5 API price while improving reasoning and long-task completion.

data.name: Xing4.0 29B A4B
data.description: Xing4.0-29B-A4B is an open-weight mixture-of-experts reasoning model from China Telecom's TeleAI (the Xing line, formerly TeleChat). It activates 4B of 29B parameters per token, supports a 256K context, and targets agentic coding, tool calling and long-context engineering tasks.

data.name: GLM-5.3-FlashX
data.description: GLM-5.3-FlashX is Z.AI's high-speed inference variant for coding agents, real-time interactions, and long-running agentic workflows. AIHubMix lists it separately from GLM-5.3-Flash with its own rates and modality set.

data.name: GLM 5.3 Prime
data.description: GLM 5.3 Prime is the top reasoning tier of Z.ai's GLM 5.3 line, above the Flash and FlashX cuts, with a 1M-token context window. It sits alongside z-ai/glm-5.3 and z-ai/glm-5.3-flash as a separately priced official variant rather than a packaging of them, so it keeps its own listing row.
